<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR adds a new HiCache host memory layout: `page_blob_direct`. This is a preparatory PR for the Tensorcast HiCache backend integration https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27265. The Tensorcast backend wants a page-major host layout where each logical cache page is represented as one contiguous page blob.  As requested by @hzh0425, splitting this layout support into a separate PR keeps the Tensorcast backend PR focused on the backend itself.

The main advantages of `page_blob_direct` layout are stated in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27265 ("page_blob_direct layout" part). Besides, it becomes a unified HiCache host-layout option across MHA, MLA, and Mamba models, while preserving each cache type's native physical representation.

## Modifications

`page_blob_direct` essentially swaps `(page_num, 2)` positions in `page_first_direct` layout

For MHA KV cache, `page_blob_direct` stores host KV cache as:

  ```text
  kv_buffer shape:

    [page_num, 2, layer_num, page_size, head_num, head_dim]

  Conceptually, each logical page is laid out as one contiguous blob:

  page 0
  +--------------------------------------------------------------+
  | K for all layers/tokens/heads | V for all layers/tokens/heads |
  +--------------------------------------------------------------+

  page 1
  +--------------------------------------------------------------+
  | K for all layers/tokens/heads | V for all layers/tokens/heads |
  +--------------------------------------------------------------+

  page 2
  +--------------------------------------------------------------+
  | K for all layers/tokens/heads | V for all layers/tokens/heads |
  +--------------------------------------------------------------+

  In pointer form:

  page_blob(p) = base + p * (2 * page_bytes)

  K(p) = page_blob(p)
  V(p) = page_blob(p) + page_bytes
```
For MLA or Mamba cache, `page_blob_direct` is interpreted as the closest page-major direct layout for each cache type, one blob per page.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body: @huangtingwei9988 pls take a review for this new layout

I understand there's no fundamental difference between `page_blob_direct ` and `page_first_direct`. Where are the optimization points? Or could we improve `page_first_direct` instead of introducing another layout? @zhou-yuhan

> I understand there's no fundamental difference between `page_blob_direct ` and `page_first_direct`. Where are the optimization points? Or could we improve `page_first_direct` instead of introducing another layout? @zhou-yuhan

Yes, there's no "fundamental" difference, but `page_blob_direct` brings three advantages (copied from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27265, since this layout is introduced for TensorcastStore backend but can generally benefit other backends)
- In architectural design: decouple the internal structure of each KV page from the distributed storage/transfer backend. Backends do not and should not comprehend the internal structure of a KV page corresponding to tokens (especially with more incoming attention variants) — they only manage storage and transfer. By keeping that structure inside HiCache, it becomes much easier to support more attention variants (e.g. MLA, Mamba2) without changing the storage-side protocol.
- Performance: cut the control-plane overhead of batch_[exists|set|get] calls roughly in half for MHA. The backend side gets one slot/region offset per page instead of one per K-shard plus one per V-shard, which directly halves the scatter-gather descriptors and per-page bookkeeping in the RDMA path. The benchmarked performance gain is shown in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26702

I think simply merging k and v together yields negligible benefits, and this only applies to regular MHA, not Asymmetric MHA. If you do see an improvement in your scenario, you can simply change the `dim` of the MHA's `page-first-direct` to `[page-num, 2, layer-num, ...]` instead of introducing a new layout.

OK. We will try to refactor https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27265 to reuse the existing `page_first_direct` layout. Thank you for your attention and feedback!

Reopen it if the work is still relevant.

`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`

`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a new host memory layout called "page_blob_direct" across the cache controller, memory pool host, and MHA pool host, along with corresponding unit tests. The reviewer feedback highlights a few key improvements: first, the existing "page_first_direct" layout should be updated similarly to "page_blob_direct" in "memory_pool_host.py" and "mha.py" to prevent slicing the page dimension instead of the layer dimension; second, "page_first_direct" should be included in the "is_page_first_layout" check in "cache_controller.py" for consistency; and finally, a redundant modulo check for "stride" in "mha.py" can be simplified.

+"""Unit tests for the page_blob_direct host layout."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool_host import MambaPoolHost, MLATokenToKVPoolHost
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.mha import MHATokenToKVPoolHost
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class PageBlobDirectLayoutTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def _build_mha_pool(self) -> MHATokenToKVPoolHost:
+        device_pool = SimpleNamespace(
+            head_num=2,
+            head_dim=3,
+            layer_num=4,
+            layer_shard_enabled=False,
+            store_dtype=torch.float16,
+            size=2,
+            start_layer=0,
+            end_layer=4,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+        return MHATokenToKVPoolHost(
+            device_pool,
+            host_to_device_ratio=2.0,
+            host_size=0,
+            page_size=2,
+            layout="page_blob_direct",
+            pin_memory=False,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+
+    def test_mha_page_blob_direct_keeps_page_blob_contiguous(self) -> None:
+        pool = self._build_mha_pool()
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            tuple(pool.kv_buffer.shape),
+            (
+                pool.page_num,
+                2,
+                pool.layer_num,
+                pool.page_size,
+                pool.head_num,
+                pool.head_dim,
+            ),
+        )
+
+        page = torch.arange(pool.get_dummy_flat_data_page().numel(), dtype=pool.dtype)
+        pool.set_from_flat_data_page(0, page)
+
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(pool.get_data_page(0, flat=True), page))
+
+        first_page_indices = torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int64)
+        ptrs, sizes = pool.get_page_buffer_meta(first_page_indices)
+        self.assertEqual(len(ptrs), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(sizes, [sizes[0], sizes[0]])
+        self.assertEqual(ptrs[1] - ptrs[0], sizes[0])
+
+        two_page_indices = torch.tensor([0, 1, 2, 3], dtype=torch.int64)
+        ptrs, sizes = pool.get_page_buffer_meta(two_page_indices)
+        self.assertEqual(len(ptrs), 4)
+        self.assertEqual(ptrs[2] - ptrs[0], 2 * sizes[0])
+
+    def test_mla_page_blob_direct_matches_direct_page_shape(self) -> None:
+        device_pool = SimpleNamespace(
+            kv_lora_rank=8,
+            qk_rope_head_dim=4,
+            layer_num=3,
+            layer_shard_enabled=False,
+            store_dtype=torch.float16,
+            size=2,
+            start_layer=0,
+            end_layer=3,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+        pool = MLATokenToKVPoolHost(
+            device_pool,
+            host_to_device_ratio=2.0,
+            host_size=0,
+            page_size=2,
+            layout="page_blob_direct",
+            pin_memory=False,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            tuple(pool.kv_buffer.shape),
+            (
+                pool.page_num,
+                pool.layer_num,
+                pool.page_size,
+                1,
+                pool.kv_cache_dim,
+            ),
+        )
+
+        page = torch.arange(pool.get_dummy_flat_data_page().numel(), dtype=pool.dtype)
+        pool.set_from_flat_data_page(0, page)
+
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(pool.get_data_page(0, flat=True), page))
+
+        first_page_indices = torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int64)
+        ptrs, sizes = pool.get_page_buffer_meta(first_page_indices)
+        self.assertEqual(len(ptrs), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(len(sizes), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(sizes[0], page.numel() * page.element_size())
+
+        two_page_indices = torch.tensor([0, 1, 2, 3], dtype=torch.int64)
+        ptrs, sizes = pool.get_page_buffer_meta(two_page_indices)
+        self.assertEqual(len(ptrs), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(ptrs[1] - ptrs[0], sizes[0])
+
+    def test_mamba_page_blob_direct_uses_direct_page_shape(self) -> None:
+        device_pool = SimpleNamespace(
+            num_mamba_layers=2,
+            size=3,
+            device="cpu",
+            mamba_cache=SimpleNamespace(
+                temporal=torch.zeros((2, 3, 5), dtype=torch.float16),
+                conv=[torch.zeros((2, 3, 4), dtype=torch.float16)],
+            ),
+        )
+        pool = MambaPoolHost(
+            device_pool,
+            host_to_device_ratio=1.0,
+            host_size=0,
+            layout="page_blob_direct",
+            pin_memory=False,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(pool.temporal_buffer.shape), (pool.size, 2, 1, 5))
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(pool.conv_buffer[0].shape), (pool.size, 2, 1, 4))
+
+        page = torch.arange(pool.get_dummy_flat_data_page().numel(), dtype=torch.uint8)
+        pool.set_from_flat_data_page(0, page)
+
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(pool.get_data_page(0, flat=True), page))
+
+        ptrs, sizes = pool.get_page_buffer_meta(torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int64))
+        self.assertEqual(len(ptrs), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(len(sizes), 2)
+
+

+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body: @huangtingwei9988 pls take a review for this new layout

I understand there's no fundamental difference between `page_blob_direct ` and `page_first_direct`. Where are the optimization points? Or could we improve `page_first_direct` instead of introducing another layout? @zhou-yuhan

> I understand there's no fundamental difference between `page_blob_direct ` and `page_first_direct`. Where are the optimization points? Or could we improve `page_first_direct` instead of introducing another layout? @zhou-yuhan

Yes, there's no "fundamental" difference, but `page_blob_direct` brings three advantages (copied from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27265, since this layout is introduced for TensorcastStore backend but can generally benefit other backends)
- In architectural design: decouple the internal structure of each KV page from the distributed storage/transfer backend. Backends do not and should not comprehend the internal structure of a KV page corresponding to tokens (especially with more incoming attention variants) — they only manage storage and transfer. By keeping that structure inside HiCache, it becomes much easier to support more attention variants (e.g. MLA, Mamba2) without changing the storage-side protocol.
- Performance: cut the control-plane overhead of batch_[exists|set|get] calls roughly in half for MHA. The backend side gets one slot/region offset per page instead of one per K-shard plus one per V-shard, which directly halves the scatter-gather descriptors and per-page bookkeeping in the RDMA path. The benchmarked performance gain is shown in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26702

I think simply merging k and v together yields negligible benefits, and this only applies to regular MHA, not Asymmetric MHA. If you do see an improvement in your scenario, you can simply change the `dim` of the MHA's `page-first-direct` to `[page-num, 2, layer-num, ...]` instead of introducing a new layout.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a new host memory layout called "page_blob_direct" across the cache controller, memory pool host, and MHA pool host, along with corresponding unit tests.
